advertisement dated 05.10.2021.

counter affidavit.

the counsel for the petitioner to file rejoinder 
affidavit.

Instructor (Mechanical) shall be subject to the

06.12.2024 WPSS No. 1448 of 2024
Sri Rakesh Thapliyal, J.
1. Mr. Vinay Kumar, learned counsel for the 
petitioner.
2. Mr. Amarendra Pratap Singh, learned Additional 
Advocate General assisted by Mr. Pradeep Hairiya, 
learned Standing Counsel for the State.
3. Mr. B.D. Pande, learned counsel for respondent 
no.3.
4. Put up this matter on 10.12.2024, as a first 
case.
5. On that day, the State may get instructions in 
the matter whether the recruiting body has a right to 
reject the candidature of a candidate, who was 
permitted to participate in the examination.
6. In this particular case, twice verification of 
experience certificate was done, and the petitioner was 
placed in the tentative merit list, but again on another 
complaint, it appears that the officials of the recruiting 
body inquired from the public, and has drawn a 
presumption that the factory was not found in the 
location.
7. Let the recruiting body place before this Court 
the inquiry report furnished by a three Member 
Committee.
 (Rakesh Thapliyal, J.)

COURT’S OR JUDGE’S ORDERS
WPSS No.1448 of 2024
WPSS No.117 of 2024
Hon’ble Rakesh Thapliyal, J.
1. Mr. Vinay Kumar, learned counsel for the 
petitioner.
2. Mr. S.N. Babulkar, learned Advocate 
General assisted by Mr. C.S. Rawat, learned 
C.S.C. and Mr. Rajeev Singh Bisht, learned Addl. 
C.S.C. as well as Mr. P.S. Bisht, learned Addl. 
C.S.C. for the State. 
3. Mr. B.D. Pande, Ms. Priyanka Agarwal and 
Mr. Virendra Singh Rawat, learned counsel for 
respondent no.3/UKSSSC.
4. In the instant writ petitions, the procedures 
adopted by the recruiting body, i.e. UKSSSC is 
under scrutiny. 
5. Today, the Secretary to the Department as 
well as Chairman of recruiting body also joined 
the proceedings through video conferencing. 
6. Mr. S.N. Babulkar, learned Advocate 
General assisted by Mr. C.S. Rawat, learned 
C.S.C. and Mr. Rajeev Singh Bisht, learned Addl. 
C.S.C. as well as Mr. P.S. Bisht, learned Addl. 
C.S.C. argued the matter at length and submits 
that they may be granted time to get instructions 
in order to point out categorically the procedure 
required to be adopted by the recruiting body. 
7. On the previous date, learned State 
Counsel placed before this Court the Uttarakhand 
Act No.20 of 2014 i.e. The Uttarakhand 
Subordinate Service Selection Commission Act, 
2014 as well as the Rules framed by the 
Commission by invoking the powers conferred by 
Section 23 of Act No.20 of 2014 and this Court 
examined all the provisions of the Act as well as  the Regulations and there is no such provision, 
which empowered the recruiting body to prepare 
a provisional list and to publish the same in the 
website. 
8. Section 18 of the Act clearly provides that 
after receiving the requisition, the recruiting body 
after scrutinizing the applications shall proceed
with the written examination or interview,
whatever it is and then prepare a select list and 
forward it to the Appointing Authority. There is 
no such provision for publication of merit list in 
the website. 
9. Surprisingly, in this particular case, thrice 
the provisional merit list was published in the 
website and thereafter certain news items were 
got viral on the social media on which the 
recruiting body referred the matter to vigilance 
establishment and also constituted a committee 
to examine the genuineness of the testimonials 
of some of the candidates. Thereafter, again 
recruiting body received some more complaints 
from different sources and thereafter result of 14 
candidates were put on hold. Thereafter, again a 
three members committee was constituted and 
the said committee submitted its report, which is 
reflected from the show cause notices issued to 
the candidates wherein it is mentioned that the 
Commission from its own level through enquiry 
committee carried physical verification of the 
concerned firms, but the Committee does not 
find the firms in the given address and local 
peoples also inform that they have no knowledge 
of firms from which it reveals that firm is not 
established in the given address.
10. It is very surprising and very shocking that 
in mid of selection process, the news relating to 
select list got viral in social media. It should not 
be happened because once Government sent a 
requisition to the recruiting body, then secrecy  and transparency of selection has to be 
maintained.
11. Apart from this, what this Court observed 
that by publishing the provisional merit list in the 
website on different stages without forwarding it 
to the Appointing Authority inviting objections 
from the candidates, who participated in the 
selection process, wholly impermissible and 
unwarranted. Who are responsible for this? This 
Court will also go into this question. 
12. Now the question is whether in the mid of 
selection process, recruiting body can invite 
objections from candidates, particularly, when 
the selection is on the way and no select list was 
sent to the Government/Appointing Authority as 
per mandate of Section 18 of Act No.20 of 2014. 
13. After gone through the provisions of 
Uttarakhand Act No.20 of 2014, i.e. the 
Uttarakhand Subordinate Service Selection 
Commission Act, 2014, as well as the entire 
Rules framed by the Commission by invoking 
power, as conferred by Section 23, and further 
the procedure, as adopted by the respondent￾Commission, primarily, this Court is of the view 
that the Commission failed to maintain the 
secrecy of selection, which itself is reflected from 
Annexure-10, the press note dated 29.01.2024, 
wherein there is a reference that the news 
relating to selection, in question, got viral in 
social media. Therefore, this Court is taking very 
serious view in the matter, for which, this Court 
wants the assistance of learned Advocate 
General. Therefore, this Court is framing certain 
questions, so that the learned Advocate General 
may address on these issues.
i. Whether the Uttarakhand Subordinate Service 
Selection Commission was right in publishing 
provisional merit list in its website for the 
purpose of inviting objections and 
representations from the candidates, as it is  reflected from the advertisement dated 
25.10.2023 (Annexure-6), advertisement dated 
10.11.2023 (Annexure-7), and advertisement 
dated 08.01.2024 (Annexure-8).
ii. Whether Section 18 of the Uttarakhand Act 
No.20 of 2014 empowers the Commission to 
publish provisional merit lists in its website, to 
forward the one select list to the Appointing 
Authority.
iii. Whether the Commission was right to 
entertain the complaints received from different 
sources (as reflected from press note dated 
29.01.2024) in mid of the selection process, 
particularly, when the select list was not 
forwarded to the Appointing Authority as per 
Section 18 of the Act.
iv. Whether the Commission was right in 
constituting a Committee for verifying the 
location of firm to ascertain the genuineness of 
certificates of the candidates, and based on the 
said report, selection of petitioners put on hold.
14. Apart from this, the extract of Paragraph 
No.3 of notice dated 11.06.2024 is being 
extracted here-in-below so that learned Advocate 
General may also address on this.

time to get complete instructions in the matter, 
as well as to file an affidavit.
16. Time, so prayed for, is granted.

COURT’S OR JUDGES’S ORDERS
WPSS No. 1448 of 2024
With
WPSS No. 117 of 2024
WPSS No. 224 of 2024
Hon’ble Rakesh Thapliyal, J.
1. Mr. Vinay Kumar, learned counsel for the 
petitioner, Mr. S.N. Babulkar, learned Advocate 
General, assisted by Mr. C.S. Rawat, learned Chief 
Standing Counsel and Mr. Rajeev Singh Bisht, learned 
Additional Chief Standing Counsel and Mr. Pradeep 
Hairiya, learned Standing Counsel for the State and 
Mr. B.D. Pande, learned counsel for UKSSSC.
2. In all these writ petitions, on the 
previous date i.e. on 13.12.2024, this Court framed 
four questions, which are being reproduced 
herein:-
“13. After gone through the provisions of 
Uttarakhand Act No.20 of 2014, i.e. the 
Uttarakhand Subordinate Service Selection 
Commission Act, 2014, as well as the entire Rules 
framed by the Commission by invoking power, as 
conferred by Section 23, and further the 
procedure, as adopted by the respondent
Commission, primarily, this Court is of the view 
that the Commission failed to maintain the 
secrecy of selection, which itself is reflected from 
Annexure-10, the press note dated 29.01.2024, 
wherein there is a reference that the news 
relating to selection, in question, got viral in social 
media. Therefore, this Court is taking very serious 
view in the matter, for which, this Court wants 
the assistance of learned Advocate General. 
Therefore, this Court is framing certain questions, 
so that the learned Advocate General may 
address on these issues.
“i.Whether the Uttarakhand Subordinate Service 
Selection Commission was right in publishing 
provisional merit list in its website for the purpose  of inviting objections and representations from 
the candidates, as it is reflected from the 
advertisement dated 25.10.2023 (Annexure-6), 
advertisement dated 10.11.2023 (Annexure-7), 
and advertisement dated 08.01.2024 (Annexure￾8). 
ii. Whether Section 18 of the Uttarakhand Act 
No.20 of 2014 empowers the Commission to 
publish provisional merit lists in its website, to 
forward the one select list to the Appointing 
Authority. 
iii. Whether the Commission was right to 
entertain the complaints received from different 
sources (as reflected from press note dated 
29.01.2024) in mid of the selection process, 
particularly, when the select list was not 
forwarded to the Appointing Authority as per 
Section 18 of the Act.
iv. Whether the Commission was right in 
constituting a Committee for verifying the 
location of firm to ascertain the genuineness of 
certificates of the candidates, and based on the 
said report, selection of petitioners put on hold.”
3. In pre-lunch session, Mr. Pradeep 
Hairiya, learned Standing Counsel, give the answer of 
all the questions as above in ‘No’. On that date, the 
Commission was also directed to place before this 
Court the details of the members of the Expert 
Committee as well as their report in the sealed 
envelope, but, despite this, they have not complied 
with the order and have not produced the report in 
the sealed envelope.
4. After gone through the provisions of the 
Uttarakhand Act No. 20 of 2024 and the Regulations 
framed by the Commission by invoking the powers 
conferred by Section 23 of the Act, the Court was of 
the view that the Commission has no power to 
publish the provisional merit list in it’s website since  by virtue of Section 18 of the Act, the Commission 
have to send the select list to the Government, but, 
surprisingly in these cases, what has happened,
thrice the provisional merit list was published in the 
website for inviting objections from the candidate 
and during mid of selection process, some news got 
viral in the social media and the Recruiting Body took 
cognizance on that and thereafter Recruiting Body 
received some more complaints and then constitute 
a Committee.
5. Today, certain written instructions have 
been placed before this Court by Mr. B.D. Pandey,
learned counsel for the Commission and one 
document is the office memorandum dated 
21.11.2024, which pertains to the Constitution of the 
Committee of five persons for verifying the 
certificates of some candidates.
6. This written instruction also contains a 
report and from the report, it reveals that after spot￾inspection, the Committee submitted it’s report.
7. It is very strange that in mid of selection 
process, the Recruiting Body gave the task to a 
Committee to verify certificate after visiting the site 
to examine whether that establishment from where 
the certificates have been issued are located in place 
or not.
8. After gone through the written 
instruction and observation, as recorded in my  previous order, it appears that the Recruiting Body 
could not maintain the secrecy of the selection, 
which is evident from the fact that thrice the 
provisional list was published in the website inviting 
the objections from candidates. To maintain the 
secrecy of the selection is the prime duty of the 
Recruiting Body, which they have failed to do so and 
this is the very serious issue because since last so 
many years, various selections were carried out by 
the Recruiting Bodies, but, there is no transparency 
and in mid of the selection, so many litigants 
approach to this Court questioning the manner in
which the Recruiting Body proceed with the selection 
process. This is really very shocking, which certainly 
requires deep scrutiny.
9. Put up this matter on 03.01.2025, on top 
of Board, keeping the matter as part heard.
10. By that time, the Commission shall 
produce the records relating to the selection process 
including the decision for taking cognizance on the 
news, which got viral in social media including the 
details of the complaints received and the report of 
the Expert Committee including details of each 
member of the Committee constituted.
(Rakesh Thapliyal, J.)
 27.12.2024
Ujjwal

1. Mr. M.C. Pant, Mr. Vinay Kumar, Mr. 
Pramod Bailwal and Mr. Tapan Singh, learned 
counsel for the petitioners, Mr. Pradeep Hairiya, 
learned Standing Counsel for the State and Mr. B.D. 
Pande, learned counsel for respondent no. 3.
2. Mr. Pradeep Hairiya, learned Standing 
Counsel in order to assist this Court placed before 
this Court one of the Government Order dated 
13.03.2024, which clearly provides, at what stage 
the document verification has to be done.
3. On perusal of this Government Order, it 
reveals that the Recruiting Body are exceeding their 
powers and jurisdiction, due to which, there is no 
secrecy and transparency in the selection  conducted by the recruiting body. This is a case in 
which a news item with regard to these selections 
got viral in the social media and thereafter so many 
complaints have been received and thereafter, the 
Recruiting Body constituted a Committee for the 
purposes of spot inspection and the members of 
the Committee inquired by visiting the site and get 
the statement of the local people and submit the 
report.
4. Since, the entire functioning of the 
Recruiting Bodies is under scrutiny, therefore, put 
up this matter on 09.01.2025 at 04:00 p.m.,
treating WPSS No. 1448 of 2024 as the leading one.
Copy of this order be placed in the file of each of 
the connected matters.
(Rakesh Thapliyal, J.)

Hon’ble Rakesh Thapliyal, J.
1. Mr. Vinay Kumar, Mr. Tapan Singh, Mr. M.C. 
Pant, Mr. Pramod Bailwal, learned counsel for the 
appellant.
2. Mr. C. S. Rawat, learned Chief Standing Counsel 
for the State.
3. Ms. Devika Tiwari, Mr. B.D. Pandey and Mr. 
Shivam Raturi, learned counsel, holding brief of Mr. 
Shailendra Nauriyal, learned counsels for the UKSSSC. 
4. Ms. Devika Tiwari, learned counsel for the 
UKSSSC is directed to assist this Court on behalf of the 
UKSSSC – Recruiting Agency on the next date. 
5. A counter affidavit has been filed by the 
Recruiting Agency but as per counsel for the 
petitioners, statements given in the counter affidavit 
are contrary to the Act and Regulation. If it is so, then it 
is a very serious issue.
6. Ms. Devika Tiwari, learned counsel for the
Recruiting Agency undertakes before this Court that 
she will properly assist this Court and she will sit with 
the Panel Lawyers of the Recruiting Agency and do 
some research work and she will file better affidavit, if 
so required, within fifteen days. 
7. Since procedure adopted by the Recruiting 
Agency is under scrutiny in all these writ petitions, 
therefore, learned Chief Standing Counsel should also 
assist this Court and may also file additional affidavit, 
only with regard to the procedure, which is being 
followed by the recruiting agency. 
8. List on 25.03.2025 at 02.00 p.m.

continue till the next date of listing.

COURT’S OR JUDGES’S ORDERS
WPSS No. 1448 of 2024
And connected matters
Hon’ble Rakesh Thapliyal, J.
1. Mr. Niranjan Bhatt, Mr. Vinay Kumar, Mr. Tapan 
Singh and Mr. M.C. Pant, learned counsel for the 
petitioners.
2. Mr. Pradeep Hairiya, learned Standing Counsel 
for the State.
3. Ms. Devika Tiwari, learned counsel for the 
respondent.
4. Chairman and the Secretary are also present in 
order to assist this court and they place before this 
court the guidelines.
5. Put up this matter on 04.04.2025 at 2:00 PM to 
examine the following issues:
(i) Whether the recruiting/selecting body has a 
right to reject the candidature of a candidate after 
permitting him to participate in the examination 
on the ground of the eligibility?
(ii) Whether the guidelines framed by the 
Commission in the year 2015 have a statutory 
force particularly in view of Section 15(2) of the 
Act when the guidelines apparently are
inconsistent with the Act and the Rules?
(iii) Whether the Commission/Selecting body was 
right in publishing the provisional merit list 
thrice in this case particularly in view of Section 
18 of the Uttarakhand Act No. 20 of 2014?
(iv) Whether while preparing the merit list the 
eligibility of a candidate has to be seen or only 
the marks obtained in the examination?
(v) Whether the eligibility of a candidate has to be 
scrutinized at once that too before the 
commencement of the written examination or till 
the conclusion of the selection?
(vi) Whether the Commission was right in 
entertaining the complaints of the candidates 
that too after the commencement of the written  examination i.e. after issuance of the first 
provisional merit list dated 17.04.2023?
(vii) Whether the State Government was right in 
intervening in the mid of the selection on the 
request of the commission to depute their 
officials for examining the genuineness of the 
certificate of the candidates?
(viii) Whether selecting body was right in sending 
select list in part followed by their appointment
particularly when the eligibility of some of the 
candidates who have permitted to participate in 
the written examination were under scrutiny?
6. In the meantime, learned counsel for the 
selecting body shall prepare compilation of the Act, 
Rules and the Guidelines.
7. For the time being the personal appearance of the 
officers are exempted.
 
 (Rakesh Thapliyal, J.)
 02.04.2025
